findings.explanation: The root explicitly connects manuscript, analysis, data subdatasets and the container. Following registered REMoDNaV links reaches benchmark annotations. Excluding the upstream acquisition-only local-path repository is defensible because the analysis consumes exported eye-gaze files, not its contents.

The analysis identifies benchmark MAT files, studyforrest exported samples and event TSVs through the linked modules. Required source and input references are present even though cohort payload bytes are absent; the latter is not a discoverability defect.

The container recipe specifies tool/library families, the invocation selects an image and temporary HOME, and CLI/default parameters are inspectable. Moving dependency resolution affects D-03 rather than ingredient inclusion.

Distinct root, implementation, raw-data and benchmark declarations are reachable through root/module paths. The label module inventory supplies no attributable license declaration, sufficient to prevent complete coverage. Uninspected container bytes should be described as unresolved license coverage rather than proved absence of installed notices.

The root tree records source blobs and gitlinks; frozen inventories record annex keys for data and image blobs. These identify intended bytes independently of whether retrieval was attempted. Floating build inputs are distinct from the selected frozen image.

Git trees recursively select modules and git-annex pointers identify large data and image content. This is a compatible root-resolvable tracking structure for the scoped research components; the assessment does not mistake an ordinary latest image tag for its actual identity.

Root and linked histories inspected in the frozen corpus contain author, dates and change descriptions across code, data, results and image changes. Such attribution does not establish authenticated identity, appropriately left to T-06.

The two DataLad records explicitly contain commands, input selections, outputs and recorded exit status. The quality calculation remains outside the CLI and the manuscript build has instructions rather than an identified complete run record, so all-step programmatic coverage is not established.

The paper run records its image input and is tied to a versioned state. The label-generation record invokes host Python with PYTHONPATH but identifies no exact environment image or locked package set. This is a concrete limit on execution-version coverage, supporting the partial anchor.

Read-only inspection of the cached results-containerized tag confirms a PGP signature and the stated target. Neither tag text nor README provides a signer-key trust/identity verification route. The zero anchor explicitly permits this situation; the review did not attempt cryptographic verification.

The root supplies clone, prerequisites and rerun instructions; the run selects benchmark, all relevant raw eye-gaze patterns, label TSVs and the image. The raw module also explains annex initialization/get. The acquisition specification is adequately described without claiming present-day successful downloads.

Registered nested modules, root gitlinks, analysis paths and the container/build configuration specify which components connect. The acquisition-only local source repository does not enter the paper runtime assembly.
